note: SHA-256 fingerprints of credentials known to have been exposed. AEON refuses to run with any of these and rotates them at launch. Storing a hash is safe: these are high-entropy random values, so the digest reveals nothing and cannot be reversed. NEVER put a raw secret in this file.
why: BO-A3b. AEON_MOBILE_SECRET appeared in a transcript and remained a valid credential for the headless path. It was owed rotation across three build orders and survived every one, because rotation was a manual step nobody was blocked by. The install was deleted and re-cloned on 2026-08-03, which would have generated a fresh secret — except the preserved .env carries the exposed value, and that .env MUST be restored for the vault master key. The restore path therefore re-introduced the leak. A fingerprint denylist closes it with no operator action at all.

credentials.reason: present in a chat transcript; carried forward in Desktop\AEON-credentials-2026-08-02\.env
